item.title: Altercation between female Police officer and street kid in Mark Street, calls made for authorities to act regarding ongoing street kids issue
item.description: The streets of Suva City like Mark Street now have a number of street kids hassling people almost on a daily basis. Many people continue to contact fijivillage News about this, and are calling on the authorities to take action.
item.content:encoded:
The streets of Suva City like Mark Street now have a number of street kids hassling people almost on a daily basis.

Many people continue to contact fijivillage News about this, and are calling on the authorities to take action.

At lunch time today, there was an altercation between a female Police Officer and a street kid along Mark Street when the officer intervened to stop one of the street kids hassling members of the public.

People are calling for immediate action as they say there is a rise in these activities where street kids are hassling and even robbing people.

Most of these street kids are of school age.

Under compulsory education provisions in the Education Act approved by parliament in May this year, parents whose children are not enrolled in school can be fined up to $500, face imprisonment for up to 2 months, or both.

According to the Education Act 2025, the Permanent Secretary is responsible for ensuring compliance and may issue directives to parents, including legal guardians, if a child is not enrolled or attending school.

Exemptions may be granted by the Minister for valid reasons, and school heads are required to report any non-compliance to the Permanent Secretary.

We have contacted Police, Minister for Education Aseri Radrodro and Ministry for Children Sashi Kiran.

Police Chief of Operations, ACP Kasiano Vusonilawe says their divisional operations team has been directed to enforce the Minor Offences Act to curb such incidents.

He adds Police support the operations headed by the Ministry of Social Welfare in the removal of homeless people from the streets, and with street kids there have been several operations conducted to return street children and youths to their homes.

ACP Vusonilawe says a holistic approach is needed and Police are involved.

The Minister for Education and the Minister for Children are yet to comment.

item.title: Raised with Love, now giving love: Youth pastor Nancy Cakacaka shares her story on fijivillage HerStory at 7pm Wednesday
item.description: Nancy Cakacaka is a senior pastor’s wife, a youth pastor, a mentor and a woman dedicated to shaping the next generation. Lovingly known as Aunty Nancy by many young people in her community, she has devoted much of her life to guiding youths, strengthening their Christian faith and encouraging them to make positive choices.
item.content:encoded:
Nancy Cakacaka is a senior pastor’s wife, a youth pastor, a mentor and a woman dedicated to shaping the next generation.

Lovingly known as Aunty Nancy by many young people in her community, she has devoted much of her life to guiding youths, strengthening their Christian faith and encouraging them to make positive choices.

On this week’s fijivillage HerStory with Temalesi Vono, Nancy opens up about her own journey, from growing up in Bua with her grandparents after her parents separated, to the values of love, faith and discipline that shaped her upbringing.

She also shares her experiences working with young people, the challenges families and youths face today, and her message to young people to listen to their parents, stay grounded in their faith and know that they are loved.

Join us at 7pm Wednesday for fijivillage HerStory with Temalesi Vono, as we hear Aunty Nancy's story.

item.title: Visa period to Australia to be made longer for businesspeople and simplified processes expected for those who have previously held an Australian visa
item.description: Some good news as Fijians who wish to travel to Australia may have a longer stay, easier and flexible visa after the implementation of the Vuvale Union which is expected to make travel between the two countries easier. This was highlighted by the Australian High Commissioner to Fiji, Peter Roberts during the fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan when questioned on Fijians calling for visa f
item.content:encoded:
Some good news as Fijians who wish to travel to Australia may have a longer stay, easier and flexible visa after the implementation of the Vuvale Union which is expected to make travel between the two countries easier.

This was highlighted by the Australian High Commissioner to Fiji, Peter Roberts during the fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan when questioned on Fijians calling for visa free travel to Australia for years.

The High Commissioner says Australia has a universal visa system whereby anyone who travels to Australia must have a visa.

However, Roberts says under the Vuvale Union, regulatory changes will be made to extend the time that people are able to stay on a visitor visa, especially for business visas.

He says business travellers will also have the opportunity to apply for multiple-entry visas valid for up to five years.

He says they will also be working to simplify the visa application processes, particularly for people who have previously held an Australian visa and applicants may no longer have to repeatedly provide the same information each time they apply.

The High Commissioner says this will also allow Fijians to travel to Australia and return to Fiji more easily and for longer periods, while also encouraging more Australians to visit Fiji, invest and bring their skills to the country.

item.title: Nadroga Navosa Chamber calls for justice after death of 38-year-old man
item.description: Chamber President Suresh Naidu says the Chamber strongly condemns the violence and is calling on Police and the prosecution to ensure that all individuals involved are dealt with according to the law. The Chamber says there should be no partiality, bias or unfair leniency in the handling of the case.
item.content:encoded:
Chamber President Suresh Naidu says the Chamber strongly condemns the violence and is calling on Police and the prosecution to ensure that all individuals involved are dealt with according to the law.

The Chamber says there should be no partiality, bias or unfair leniency in the handling of the case.

They say violence of this nature affects not only families but also the safety and economic wellbeing of the wider community.

The Chamber says it expects swift, stern and impartial justice through the legal process.

It says it will closely monitor the ongoing legal proceedings and is calling for anyone convicted over Nand’s death and the injuries suffered by his son to receive the maximum sentence provided under the law.

The Chamber says Nand’s death is a tragic loss for his family and the wider community and is urging the relevant authorities to ensure that justice is served.

Meanwhile, 38-year-old Nand has died after he was allegedly assaulted by two men in Sigatoka yesterday.
